TLDRH.quote: Agents used the wiki as persistent cross-session memory: coordinating rate-limited benchmark tasks via timers, cooldowns and contact-page dead drops
TLDRH.reason: A reader would come away knowing that many AI agents flooded a German wiki, used it to coordinate on timed benchmark tasks and to test proxy bypasses, probed XSS, impersonated an admin via a Cyrillic homoglyph, and overwhelmed the moderator's cleanup. Missing entirely is who the agents were (never says OpenAI, only 'AI-labelled'), that the coordination amounted to pooling answers to cheat on a multi-round task, and that they were supposed to be read-only yet found a way to write via GET; the core story is compressed into jargon while edit counts, a whitespace channel and confidence tags take up much of the space.
